review.brief: Validate RM39 tier 3 (charging schema move + charge_sessions -> supercharger_sessions) before archive. Read the DIFF of commits edd5c46..HEAD, not the whole module. Checks: (1) module-boundary compliance — charging must import no other module; the leader (not a worker) made the only cross-module edit, 2 SQL statements in internal/analytics/db_integration_test.go. (2) Every DB object matches the user-confirmed design: D14 confirmed the renames, D16 requires ALL FOUR catalog objects renamed (index, CHECK, pkey, unique). A mismatch is a blocker. (3) D7 statement order in the migration, and that Down reverses exactly. (4) D15 — NO watermark CHECK/DELETE and NO write to vehicle_metric_watermarks anywhere in this change; that is tier 3b. (5) The integration tests assert the expectations design.md authored up front, not whatever the implementation does. (6) The backfill replay fix in db_backfill_integration_test.go: it maps ONLY the INSERT target forward and deliberately rejects D12's search_path approach. Verify that reasoning is sound — the statement's FROM reads telemetry's table. (7) The COMMENT ON refresh added to the migration: additive only, historic migrations untouched, Down restores original text. (8) Doc-pack conventions, and that structure docs were updated in the same change (README schema column, ai/go-conventions.md, module AGENTS.md, kkpa/context KB). (9) Performance-Profile compliance: catalog-only operations, no table rewrite, index preserved. (10) Anti-gaming: no weakened acceptance criteria, no self-approved statuses, tasks append-only. Test-Execution-Policy (verbatim): 'Claude writes tests but never runs the suite — never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards. The owner runs the suite and reports results; work that is complete but unexecuted is awaiting-user-verification, never done, and a passing suite is recorded as the owner's report, never claimed by the assistant.' WHICH SIGNALS CAME FROM WHERE: go build / go vet / gofmt / all six guards / openspec validate --strict were ASSISTANT-run. The SUITE was LEADER-run under owner decision D10, which authorized it for this run only. Docker was down, so it ran against a local Postgres with each DB-backed package on its own fresh database — NOT through testcontainers. A container run is still owed. Judge test QUALITY by reading the tests; do not run them yourself.

rounds.independent_verification: Read the full historic CREATE TABLE in 20260823000001_add_charge_sessions.sql end to end: confirmed exactly 5 inline column CHECKs with no explicit CONSTRAINT name (start_battery_pct, end_battery_pct, battery_pct_source, start_battery_pct_est, end_battery_pct_est) plus the one named CHECK, the PK, and the UNIQUE -- 8 constraints total, all now renamed across round 1 (4) and round 2 (5). Confirmed the GENERATED column inferred_capacity_kwh_calc (added later) carries no CHECK. No sequence exists on this table (no serial/identity column) and no trigger is defined on it, so neither is a residual-name risk. Verified the new migration file directly: the 5 new RENAME CONSTRAINT statements in Up sit between the original 4-object block and the COMMENT ON refresh (does not disturb D7 order), and Down reverses in the exact mirror position (comments restored first, then the 5 new constraints reversed, then the original 4, then index, then table rename, then SET SCHEMA public, then DROP SCHEMA) -- byte-for-byte the opposite of Up. go build/go vet/gofmt clean; openspec validate --strict passes. Answering the coordinator's specific question -- empirically tested Postgres 16 (local Homebrew instance, in a ROLLBACK-ed transaction, no lasting effect) rather than relying on memory: ALTER TABLE ... RENAME CONSTRAINT on a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint automatically renames its backing index too (pg_indexes reflects the new name with no separate ALTER INDEX statement needed), and ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO automatically renames the implicit composite row type in pg_type. Both confirmed live, not assumed. Given that, "no pg_constraint or pg_indexes name beginning charge_sessions" (spec.md's new criterion) is the right check and this migration satisfies it completely -- I found no further catalog object this change leaves behind. The one gap found is a documentation one (F2), not a DDL one.

answers_to_coordinator.loop_vs_explicit_list: Agree with the framing as rewritten; would not switch the migration itself to a runtime catalog loop. The bug was never "explicit lists are the wrong mechanism" -- it was "the list was built by reading CREATE TABLE text instead of querying the catalog." A runtime loop over pg_constraint filtered by name LIKE 'charge_sessions%' does not actually buy more completeness than what design.md now specifies: enumerate every constraint bound to the table's OID with no name filter at all (WHERE conrelid = the table, full stop) -- which is exactly what the Test Contract's own verification query already does, and which is what should have been run before finalizing the list, not just after. A pattern-matching loop trades reviewability (a reviewer can no longer tell from reading the file what will happen) and loud failure (an absent name silently does nothing instead of erroring) for a completeness guarantee that an OID-scoped catalog query already provides at authoring time, with no runtime ambiguity. The real backstop against drift is exactly what the Test Contract now says: treat the negative catalog check (no name beginning charge_sessions) as binding in every environment the migration runs against, independent of whether the list inside the DDL is complete. Keep the explicit list; the fix is sourcing it correctly, which af5a7be already states.

rounds.answer_to_coordinator_question: Design.md's D1/D7 section is sufficient without the verbatim SQL, and I would not restore a copy. Reasoning: (1) nothing about the 'HOW' is actually lost -- the numbered order list still names every DDL verb (CREATE SCHEMA, SET SCHEMA, RENAME TO, the catalog renames, COMMENT ON) and every real object/table name in the order they run, which is the level of detail a reader needs to verify the mechanism; only the literal SQL syntax is gone, and that syntax is not what made the rationale rationale. (2) The migration file this section now points to is not an ordinary mutable source file that could drift out from under an archived design.md -- this project's own D1 rule (restated in this same design.md's 'Do NOT touch' section, in AGENTS.md, and in go-conventions.md) is that a shipped migration is NEVER edited again. That is a stronger permanence guarantee than most cross-references get, so the pointer cannot go stale the way the embedded copy did three times. (3) This is exactly the OpenSpec convention this project states elsewhere (proposal.md: 'implementation (HOW) lives in design.md') read correctly -- design.md's job is to carry the mechanism and the reasoning, not to be a second, unsynchronized copy of a file whose only job is to be that content. One optional, non-blocking suggestion: the section could say in one sentence that the pointer is safe specifically because historic migrations are never edited (D1), making the archival-standalone argument explicit rather than something a reader has to reconstruct from the 'Do NOT touch' section elsewhere in the same file. I would not hold up this round on that alone.
